items.label: S1
items.text: S1. Practical motivation, clear figures, and the pipeline diagram is helpful.

items.label: S2
items.text: S2. Code is promised to be released.

items.label: W1
items.text: I think the data split is potentially leaking: samples from the same production line appear in both train and test. If true this would invalidate the main table, and it is a fundamental problem rather than a presentation issue.

items.label: W2
items.text: The improvement on the second benchmark is about 0.6 mAP, which is within the reported noise. Statistical reliability is not established.

items.label: W3
items.text: Notation in Section 3.2 is confusing: z and \hat{z} are used interchangeably, and Eq. (4) is never referenced again.

items.label: Q1
items.text: Is the fusion module trained jointly with the diffusion backbone or frozen? This is stated in the appendix but the appendix and main text disagree.

reviewers.scoreCondition: if the authors provide a comparison against at least one 2026 method

items.label: S1
items.text: S1. The latent-space fusion formulation is elegant and avoids per-modality encoders at inference time.

items.label: S2
items.text: S2. Consistent gains over the three cited fusion baselines on both datasets.

items.label: W1
items.text: The novelty relative to cross-attention conditioning (e.g. the 2025 "AdaCond" line of work) is not clearly established. The claimed contribution looks like an incremental change of the conditioning interface. This is a major concern for me.

items.label: W2
items.text: Only two baselines are from the last 18 months. There is no comparison against a strong recent method, so I cannot judge whether the gain comes from fusion or from the backbone.

items.label: W3
items.text: No ablation on the number of fused modalities. What happens when one sensor is missing at test time? Robustness to missing modality is the whole point of the application scenario.

items.label: Q1
items.text: Could you report inference latency and peak memory relative to the early-fusion baseline? The method section does not state the overhead.

items.label: Q2
items.text: Which random seeds were used? Are the reported standard deviations over seeds or over test folds?

items.label: W4
items.text: The paper acknowledges only dataset coverage. I would consider raising my score if the authors provide a comparison against at least one 2026 method and a missing-modality ablation.

items.label: S1
items.text: S1. Clean method, strong empirical results, good presentation.

items.label: S2
items.text: S2. The missing-modality discussion in the appendix is valuable.

items.label: W1
items.text: A minor point: Table 2 should report the standard deviation of the detector-free baseline too, for symmetry.

items.label: Q1
items.text: Do you plan to release the anonymized evaluation scripts?

items.label: S1
items.text: S1. The problem formulation is well motivated and the application is meaningful.

items.label: W1
items.text: The theoretical justification in Sec. 3.3 seems to assume the latent distribution is Gaussian, which is generally false for trained VAEs. Minor for me but should be softened in the text.

items.label: W2
items.text: Related work on multi-modal fusion in medical imaging is missing; the authors should cite and discuss it.

items.label: Q1
items.text: Could you clarify the computational cost as the number of modalities grows?
